summary: The admitted v43 recording reaches apply.c:next_to_u() when a mounted Wizard presses > on a down staircase. C scans leashed monsters before checking the steed’s Amulet state, then returns true for this non-Amulet pony. The first complete source goal is a file-port of apply.c:mleashed_next2u() and next_to_u(), with async leash iteration and awaited mnexto() wired through every active caller. Fresh C evidence must cover leashed-pet handling and the Amulet-bearing-steed refusal. If next_to_u() permits the selected descent, separate dog.c:keepdogs(), losedogs(), and mon_arrive() stages still block a matching mounted transfer.

source.branch: Port both complete functions in C order: mleashed_next2u() walks each living on-map monster reached by next_to_u(); for a leashed monster outside m_next2u() range it calls mnexto(RLOC_NOMSG), checks distance again, and when the monster remains too far looks up its leash. A missing leash reports impossible and refuses; a cursed leash refuses; otherwise C clears both leash links, updates inventory, and prints the slack-leash message. next_to_u() refuses on the first refused leashed monster, then refuses when u.usteed carries the Amulet, and returns true otherwise. Preserve C traversal order, short-circuiting, messages, state changes, and random calls.
functions: apply.c:mleashed_next2u() (891-914), complete leash-follow, cursed-leash refusal, and leash-release behavior
apply.c:next_to_u() (919-928), complete monster scan and mounted-Amulet gate

artifact.c:invoke_create_portal() (1921) -> js/artifacts.js (2504): gate portal creation on next_to_u().
dig.c:digactualhole() (762) -> js/dig.js:digactualhole() (1454): refuse the hero fall through a newly dug hole when a leash blocks departure.
do.c:dodown() (1251) -> js/do.js:dodown() (2481); do.c:doup() (1336) -> js/do.js:doup() (2590); do.c:goto_level() (1567, discarded result) -> js/do.js:goto_level() (2743).
teleport.c:dotele() (1145, 1154) -> js/cmd.js (6487, 6530): both teleport command routes check companions before teleport and run the post-teleport leash check; await both calls.

dependencies: The JavaScript implementation of mon.c:get_iter_mons() in js/mon.js is synchronous. The leash predicate must await mon.c:mnexto(), so add an async iteration adapter that caches nmon before each callback, skips dead or off-map monsters, preserves list order, and stops at the first true result. Keep the existing synchronous iterator and its unrelated callers unchanged.

mon.c:mnexto() already has an async JavaScript implementation in js/mon.js. Await its RLOC_NOMSG call before rechecking m_next2u(); the C call’s void result does not remove its state-changing effects from this control flow.

The existing JavaScript owners for apply.c:get_mleash(), number_leashed(), and m_unleash() are in js/apply.js; mhitu.c:m_next2u() is in js/mhitu.js; wizard.c:mon_has_amulet() is in js/wizard.js. Recheck their relevant source behavior and reuse those owners unless source inspection finds a missing branch.

The selected mounted descent still needs a separate dog.c:keepdogs() stage after next_to_u() returns true. do.c:goto_level() calls keepdogs(FALSE); whole keepdogs() also has end.c:really_done(TRUE) and wizcmds.c:makemap_remove_mons(TRUE) callers, which js/end.js and js/wizcmds.js currently refuse.

The selected descent then needs separate dog.c:losedogs() and mon_arrive() stages. losedogs() drains gm.mydogs into mon_arrive(With_you), whose steed branch restores transfer state and returns. Whole mon_arrive() also serves Before_you and After_you from losedogs() and Wiz_arrive from wizard.c:resurrect(); those branches are outside this first apply.c goal.

mon_arrive(With_you) returns for u.usteed before mon_catchup_elapsed_time() or independent-migrant placement. migrate_to_level() and mon_catchup_elapsed_time() are not dependencies of this mounted-steed branch.

evidence: The saved queue identified synthetic/v43/v43-mounted-steed-stair-descent-pager-2-cfirst at step 165. Its provenance remains manifest challenges/manifests/v43.json (SHA-256 a4b2899d882bbae4e7283f771df1cab2f78dd6a32d7c0b19378a6d8cc5ab7400), recording challenges/cases/v43/v43-mounted-steed-stair-descent-pager-2-cfirst.session.json (SHA-256 bf2a99be1ce7847f948069f91419902d39e85ebb259933e2e8588791f1141472), and the saved evaluation accepted-57c44fa48bff87c33541a147cedd6d9a0018a494-v43.json.

The saved evaluation reports 165/166 screens, 165/166 cursors, and 3913/6320 RNG calls; JavaScript stops at step 165 with unsupported hero move: next_to_u() with a steed. The recorded C branch permits a steed without the Amulet to accompany the hero.

The selected recording’s independent action history creates and tames a saddled pony with #wizgenesis, mounts it with #ride, reaches a down staircase with #wizmap, then presses >. It has no leashed companion and does not place the Amulet on the steed, so it reaches next_to_u()’s non-Amulet steed return only.

Upstream apply.c:891-914 defines the complete mleashed_next2u() behavior. It calls m_next2u(), mnexto(..., RLOC_NOMSG), rechecks distance, obtains the matching inventory leash with get_mleash(), refuses a cursed leash, or clears both leash links and prints the slack message. Upstream apply.c:919-928 calls get_iter_mons(mleashed_next2u), then refuses an Amulet-bearing u.usteed and returns true otherwise.

A focused scan at examined commit f79ab4080d5e831bb1bdbe83a27a7c35ce0f86ac emitted 165 of 166 screens and stopped at step 165 on the mounted-steed refusal; the matching C screen says “You descend the stairs.--More--”. The scan confirms the mounted path, not leash behavior or downstream transfer completion.

The existing js/apply_next_to_u.js currently throws for a leashed monster and for a non-Amulet steed. The existing js/mon.js:mnexto() is async while get_iter_mons() accepts a synchronous predicate; asynchronous traversal and caller awaiting are required to preserve apply.c’s order and effects.

A source search of nethack-c/upstream/src shows active next_to_u() calls in allmain.c:313, artifact.c:1921, dig.c:762, do.c:1251/1336/1567, teleport.c:1145/1154/1304/1453/1506, and trap.c:643. The direct C callers are moveloop_core(), invoke_create_portal(), digactualhole(), dodown(), doup(), goto_level(), dotele(), level_tele(), domagicportal(), tele_trap(), and fall_through(). They map to the JavaScript callers listed above, including the command wiring in js/cmd.js; the async signature must be awaited at every call site.

Before the first file-port can close, add independent C recordings for leashed-pet behavior and for an Amulet-bearing mounted steed. The leash recipes must reach mleashed_next2u() through next_to_u(); cover cursed-leash refusal and uncursed leash release when mnexto() leaves the pet outside the permitted range. The Amulet recipe must show next_to_u() refusing a mount that carries the Amulet. Keep the admitted v43 recording as non-Amulet mounted reachability evidence only.

When the apply.c stage returns true for the selected v43 descent, the transfer remains unverified: do.c:goto_level() calls dog.c:keepdogs(FALSE), then dog.c:losedogs() calls dog.c:mon_arrive(With_you). Current JavaScript refuses those mounted branches. Keep these as explicit later source-goal blockers; do not claim the first goal fixes the v43 screen or completes dog.c.
